items.title: Ireland now also investigating X over Grok-made sexual images
items.description: Ireland's Data Protection Commission (DPC), the country's data protection authority, has opened a formal investigation into X over the use of the platform's Grok artificial intelligence tool to generate non-consensual sexual images of real people, including children. [...]

items.description: Researchers at ETH Zurich have tested the security of Bitwarden, LastPass, Dashlane, and 1Password password managers. The post Password Managers Vulnerable to Vault Compromise Under Malicious Server appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: Apache NiFi Vulnerability Enables Authorization Bypass
items.description: A newly disclosed high-severity vulnerability in Apache NiFi exposes systems to an authorization bypass that could allow lower-privileged users to modify restricted components. Tracked as CVE-2026-25903, the flaw impacts Apache NiFi versions 1.1.0 through 2.7.2 and has been fixed in version 2.8.0. According to the Apache NiFi security advisory, the issue arises from missing authorization checks…

items.title: Malicious Chrome Extension Steals Facebook Business Manage 2FA Codes and Analytics Data
items.description: A malicious Chrome extension that claims to help Meta Business users quietly steals Facebook Business Manager 2FA codes and analytics data, putting high‑value ad accounts at risk of takeover. items.title: Langchain Community SSRF Bypass Vulnerability Enables Access to Internal Services
items.description: A Server‑Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability has been identified in the langchain/community package, affecting versions up to 1.1.13. items.title: Apple Tests End-to-End Encrypted RCS Messaging in iOS 26.4 Developer Beta
items.description: Apple on Monday released a new developer beta of iOS and iPadOS with support for end-to-end encryption (E2EE) in Rich Communications Services (RCS) messages. items.title: 25 Vulnerabilities in Cloud Password Managers Allow Unauthorized Access and Modifications
items.description: Researchers from ETH Zurich have uncovered 25 serious vulnerabilities in three leading cloud-based password managers: Bitwarden, LastPass, and Dashlane. These flaws enable a malicious server to bypass zero-knowledge encryption claims, allowing unauthorized access, modification, and recovery of users’ stored passwords and vault data.
